topics.name: State Snapshots, History & Time Travel
topics.description: Inspecting checkpoints with get_state/get_state_history and using update_state to replay or fork.
notes: - 每个 super-step 结束后 checkpointer 保存一个 checkpoint，用 StateSnapshot 表示。
- next 为空元组 () 表示图已经执行完毕。
history = list(graph.get_state_history(config))  # 最新的在最前
- START -> A -> B -> END 的图运行一次共产生 4 个 checkpoint（包含最初的空 checkpoint）。
- update_state 会创建新的 checkpoint，不会修改原 checkpoint，也不会回滚 thread。
- 更新值会经过 reducer，所以带 reducer 的 channel 是累加而不是覆盖。
- as_node 指定这次更新被视为哪个节点产生，从而决定接下来执行哪个节点。
- Replay：用历史 checkpoint 的 config 调用 invoke(None, config)；该 checkpoint 之前的节点不重跑，之后的节点会重新执行（包括 LLM 调用和 interrupt）。
- 从最终 checkpoint（没有 next 节点）replay 不会做任何事。
- Fork：先对历史 checkpoint 调用 update_state 得到新 config，再 invoke(None, fork_config)。
before_joke = next(s for s in history if s.next == ("write_joke",))

topics.name: Durability, Fault Tolerance & Checkpointer Libraries
topics.description: Durability modes, pending writes, production checkpointers and encrypted serialization.
notes: - 调用图时可以传 durability 参数，取值 exit / async / sync（持久性由低到高）。
- exit：只在执行退出（成功、报错或 interrupt）时保存；性能最好，但进程崩溃时无法从中途恢复。
- async：下一步执行的同时异步保存；性能和持久性都不错，但进程崩溃时有小概率丢失 checkpoint。
- sync：下一步开始前同步保存；持久性最高，有一定性能开销。
- 同一 super-step 里某个节点失败时，其他成功节点的 writes 作为 pending writes 保存，恢复时不会重跑这些节点。
- InMemorySaver 随 langgraph-checkpoint 提供，用于实验；SqliteSaver 适合实验和本地流程。
- PostgresSaver、MongoDBSaver 适合生产环境；数据库实现首次使用要调用 setup()。
- 删除某个 thread 的全部 checkpoint：checkpointer.delete_thread(thread_id)。
- 给 serde 参数传入 EncryptedSerializer 即可加密所有持久化状态。
- from_pycryptodome_aes() 默认从环境变量 LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY 读取 AES 密钥。

topics.name: Long-term Memory with Store
topics.description: Namespaces, put/search, semantic search, Runtime access and memory types.
notes: - Store 保存跨 thread 的长期记忆，按 namespace（字符串元组）加 key 组织，value 是字典。
- search 的 namespace_prefix 按前缀匹配；limit 默认 10，超出部分被静默截断，可用 offset 分页。
- InMemoryStore 适合开发和测试，生产环境使用 PostgresStore 等持久化实现。
- 创建 store 时配置 index（embed、dims、fields），search 时传 query 即可按语义检索。
- put(..., index=["field"]) 只嵌入指定字段；index=False 则不嵌入，仍可读取但不能被语义搜索命中。
- compile(store=store) 后，节点通过 Runtime 参数访问 runtime.store 和 runtime.context。
- hot path 写入：新记忆立即可用，但会增加延迟；后台写入：不影响主流程延迟，但要决定触发频率。

topics.name: Managing Short-term Message History
topics.description: Trimming, deleting and summarizing messages in graph state.
notes: - checkpointer 只负责持久化 state；调用模型的节点决定把 state 里的哪些数据放进模型输入。
- 常见做法：trim、delete、summarize，或自定义过滤策略。
- trim_messages 在调用模型前裁剪消息列表，不会把消息从 state 中删除。
- 用 RemoveMessage(id=...) 从 state 中永久删除消息；该 state key 必须使用 add_messages reducer（例如 MessagesState）。
- 删除后要保证历史仍然合法：有的模型要求以 user 消息开头；带 tool call 的 assistant 消息后必须跟对应的 tool 结果。
- trim 和 delete 会丢失信息；可以用模型对旧消息做摘要，把 summary 存进 state，再删除旧消息。

questions.title: What does graph.get_state(config) return when config only contains a thread_id?

options.text: The full list of every checkpoint of the thread
Only the list of messages of the thread
A StateSnapshot for the latest checkpoint of the thread
The checkpointer object used by the graph

questions.explanation: get_state returns a StateSnapshot for the latest checkpoint of the thread, or for a specific checkpoint when a checkpoint_id is also given. The list of all checkpoints comes from get_state_history.

questions.title: The graph run below finished successfully. What does the last line print?
questions.codeSnippet:
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
graph.invoke({"foo": ""}, config)

history = list(graph.get_state_history(config))
print(history[0].next)

options.text: () because the newest snapshot is first and the graph is complete
('__start__',) because the oldest snapshot is first
None because next is only set for interrupted runs
The name of the first node of the graph

questions.explanation: get_state_history returns snapshots in reverse chronological order, so index 0 is the latest one, and an empty next tuple means the graph is complete. The ('__start__',) snapshot is the last element of the list.

questions.title: A graph START -> node_a -> node_b -> END is compiled with InMemorySaver and invoked once. How many checkpoints are saved for the thread?
questions.explanation: One checkpoint is written per super-step boundary: the empty one with START next, the one with the input, the one after node_a, and the one after node_b. Only counting node outputs would miss the first two.

questions.title: Which of the following are fields of a StateSnapshot?

options.text: values
next
tasks
api_key
token_usage

questions.explanation: A StateSnapshot has values, next, config, metadata, created_at, parent_config and tasks. API keys and token usage are not stored in it.

questions.title: Complete the call that replays the graph from the checkpoint before write_joke.
questions.codeSnippet:
history = list(graph.get_state_history(config))
before_joke = next(s for s in history if s.next == ("write_joke",))

replay_result = graph.invoke(______, before_joke.config)

options.text: None
before_joke.values
history

questions.explanation: Replay and resuming a fork use invoke(None, checkpoint_config) so execution continues from that checkpoint. Passing a new input dict would not replay the saved step.

questions.title: You replay from the checkpoint just before write_joke, a node that calls an LLM. What happens?

options.text: The earlier node is skipped and write_joke runs again, including its LLM call, so the result may differ
The cached LLM response from the first run is returned without calling the model
Every node of the graph re-executes from START
Nothing runs because replay only reads stored state

questions.explanation: Nodes before the checkpoint are not re-executed, but nodes after it re-execute, including LLM calls, API requests and interrupts. Replay does not read from a cache.

questions.title: A developer expects this call to roll the thread back and overwrite the old history. What actually happens?

options.text: The old checkpoint is modified in place and the later ones are deleted
A new checkpoint is created that branches from the old one; the original history stays intact
It raises an error because old checkpoints are read-only
The latest checkpoint is replaced by the old one

questions.explanation: update_state does not roll back a thread; it creates a new checkpoint branching from the specified one. The original execution history is preserved.

questions.title: The thread has finished with values {'foo': 'b', 'bar': ['a', 'b']}. What do the values look like after update_state?
questions.codeSnippet:
class State(TypedDict):
    foo: str
    bar: Annotated[list[str], add]

graph.update_state(config, {"foo": "c", "bar": ["c"]})
print(graph.get_state(config).values)

options.text: It raises an error because the thread is already finished

questions.explanation: update_state creates a new checkpoint and passes values through the reducers: foo has no reducer so it is overwritten, while bar uses add so it accumulates. Overwriting bar would ignore its reducer.

questions.title: Which call deletes all checkpoints stored for one thread?

options.text: checkpointer.delete_thread(thread_id)
graph.update_state(config, None)
store.delete(namespace)
graph.clear(thread_id)

questions.explanation: The docs delete a thread's checkpoints with checkpointer.delete_thread(thread_id). store.delete only removes an item from a Store, not checkpoints.

questions.title: Fill in the keyword argument that selects the durability mode for this run.

options.text: persistence
checkpoint_mode
durability
save

questions.explanation: The durability mode ("exit", "async" or "sync") is passed with the durability argument of any graph execution method.

questions.title: Which statements about LangGraph durability modes are correct?

options.text: "exit" persists changes only when the run exits (success, error or interrupt)
"async" persists while the next step runs, with a small risk of a lost checkpoint if the process crashes
"sync" writes each checkpoint before the next step starts
"exit" is the most durable mode and recovers from mid-run crashes
"sync" has no performance overhead

questions.explanation: exit is the least durable (best performance), async is in between, and sync is the most durable at the cost of some overhead. exit cannot recover from a crash mid-execution.

questions.title: Nodes X and Y run in the same super-step. X succeeds, Y raises an error. What does LangGraph do when you resume from that super-step?

options.text: It re-runs both X and Y because the super-step never completed
It discards X's output and only keeps the previous checkpoint
It cannot resume until the failing node is removed from the graph
It reuses X's stored pending writes and does not re-run X

questions.explanation: LangGraph stores pending writes from nodes that completed successfully in the failed super-step, so resuming does not re-run them. Only the failed work is retried.

questions.title: Which checkpointer libraries do the docs describe as ideal for production use?

options.text: PostgresSaver
InMemorySaver
MongoDBSaver
SqliteSaver

questions.explanation: The Postgres and MongoDB checkpointers are described as ideal for production. InMemorySaver is for experimentation and SqliteSaver for experimentation and local workflows.

questions.title: Where does the AES key used by this serializer come from by default?

options.text: A random key generated on every run
The LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY environment variable
The thread_id of the current run
A key stored inside checkpoint.db

questions.explanation: from_pycryptodome_aes reads the key from LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY unless a key argument is passed. A random per-run key would make saved checkpoints unreadable later.

questions.title: This code is run for the first time against a brand-new Postgres database and does not work. What step is missing?
questions.codeSnippet:
DB_URI = "postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres"
with PostgresSaver.from_conn_string(DB_URI) as checkpointer:
    graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)
    graph.invoke({"messages": [("user", "hi")]}, config)

options.text: The checkpointer must be created with InMemorySaver first
durability="sync" is mandatory for Postgres
checkpointer.setup() must be called the first time to create the required tables
thread_id must be removed from the config

questions.explanation: Database-backed checkpointers need their schema created before use; for Postgres you call checkpointer.setup() the first time. A thread_id is still required.

questions.title: How are memories organized inside a LangGraph Store?

options.text: By thread_id and checkpoint_id
By a namespace tuple and a key, with a dict as the value
By node name and step number
By message id only

questions.explanation: Memories are put under a namespace (a tuple such as (user_id, "memories")) with a unique key and a dictionary value. thread_id and checkpoint_id belong to the checkpointer.

questions.title: What does the last line print?
questions.codeSnippet:
store = InMemoryStore()
ns = ("1", "memories")
store.put(ns, "k1", {"food_preference": "I like pizza"})

items = store.search(ns)
print(items[0].value)

options.text: k1
('1', 'memories')
{'food_preference': 'I like pizza'}
An empty list because search needs a query

questions.explanation: search without a query lists items under the namespace, and each Item exposes the stored dict as value. The key and namespace are separate attributes.

questions.title: Items exist under ("alice", "memories") and ("alice", "preferences"). What does store.search(("alice",)) return?

options.text: Only items stored exactly under ("alice",)
Items from both sub-namespaces, because the namespace prefix matches by prefix
Only items under ("alice", "memories")
An error, because a full namespace is required

questions.explanation: namespace_prefix is matched by prefix, so ("alice",) also returns items under deeper namespaces. To restrict to one level, pass the full namespace.

questions.title: Complete the index configuration that enables semantic search in the store.

options.text: dims
limit
model
namespace

questions.explanation: The index config takes the embedding function under embed and the embedding dimensions under dims (optionally fields). limit is an argument of search, not of the index.

questions.title: In a store configured with an embedding index, what is the effect of index=False on item "b"?
questions.codeSnippet:
ns = ("user_123", "memories")
store.put(ns, "a", {"food_preference": "I love Italian cuisine"})
store.put(
    ns, "b", {"system_info": "Last updated: 2024-01-01"},
    index=False,
)

options.text: Item b is not saved at all
Item b is saved only for the current thread
Item b is encrypted before it is stored
Item b is stored and retrievable, but not embedded, so semantic search cannot find it

questions.explanation: index=False stores the item without embedding it: it remains retrievable but is not searchable by semantic query. It is not a thread-scoping or encryption option.

questions.title: Complete the line that searches long-term memory from inside a node.

options.text: checkpointer
store
context
memory

questions.explanation: When the graph is compiled with store=..., the Runtime injected into the node exposes it as runtime.store. runtime.context only carries the user-provided context such as user_id.

questions.title: Which are long-term memory types described in the LangGraph memory docs?

options.text: Semantic memory (facts)
Episodic memory (experiences)
Procedural memory (instructions)
Transient memory (GPU cache)

questions.explanation: The docs map semantic memory to facts, episodic memory to experiences and procedural memory to instructions such as the agent's system prompt. Transient GPU cache is not a memory type there.

questions.title: What is an advantage of writing memories in the background rather than in the hot path?

options.text: New memories are immediately available in the very next step
It removes the need to decide how often memories are written
It eliminates the memory-writing latency from the primary application
The agent itself decides what to remember in each turn

questions.explanation: Background writing separates memory management from application logic and removes latency from the main flow. Immediate availability and in-turn decisions are hot-path traits, and background writing still needs a trigger strategy.

questions.title: With short-term memory enabled, how is the amount of history sent to the model decided?

options.text: The checkpointer automatically sends the whole persisted state to the model
The checkpointer trims history to the model's context window
The node that calls the model chooses which state data goes into the model input
Each new thread starts from a summary created by LangGraph

questions.explanation: Persisting state does not automatically send all of it to the model; the model-calling node controls the input. That is why trimming, deleting or summarizing is done in your own graph logic.

questions.title: After this node runs, what happens to the messages stored in the graph state?
questions.codeSnippet:
def call_model(state: MessagesState):
    messages = trim_messages(
        state["messages"],
        strategy="last",
        token_counter=count_tokens_approximately,
        max_tokens=128,
        start_on="human",
        end_on=("human", "tool"),
    )
    response = model.invoke(messages)
    return {"messages": [response]}

options.text: Old messages stay in state; only the trimmed list is sent to the model and the response is appended
Messages beyond 128 tokens are permanently deleted from state
The state is replaced by the trimmed list plus the response
The checkpoint is rewritten to hold only the last message

questions.explanation: trim_messages here only shapes the model input; it does not remove messages from state. Removing messages from state requires RemoveMessage.

questions.title: Complete the node that removes all messages from the state.

options.text: None
state["messages"]
REMOVE_ALL_MESSAGES

questions.explanation: RemoveMessage(id=REMOVE_ALL_MESSAGES) clears the whole message list. A single message id only removes that one message.

questions.title: When deleting messages from state, which constraints should you make sure the remaining history satisfies?

options.text: Some providers expect the history to start with a user message
Most providers require an assistant message with tool calls to be followed by the matching tool results
LangGraph repairs invalid histories, so provider rules can be ignored
RemoveMessage must always delete an even number of messages

questions.explanation: The docs warn that the resulting history must be valid for your model provider. LangGraph does not repair it and there is no even-number rule.

questions.title: The prune node should delete the two oldest messages but RemoveMessage does not work as expected. What is the problem?

options.text: RemoveMessage can only be used inside a conditional edge
The messages key needs the add_messages reducer, for example by using MessagesState
Only the last message can be removed, never the first two
The graph must be compiled without a checkpointer

questions.explanation: RemoveMessage only works with a state key that uses the add_messages reducer, such as MessagesState's messages. A plain list key has no reducer that interprets removals.
